claims.statement: build.sh is the host build entry point: it runs `trunk build --release` in `frontend/` and then `cargo build --release --features server`, and because it does not export SKIP_TRUNK, build.rs re-runs `trunk build --release` for the same assets during the cargo build.

desktop.sh builds the Tauri app with `cargo tauri build` in `desktop/` after exporting NO_STRIP=true, because linuxdeploy bundles a binutils too old to read the .relr.dyn sections modern distributions ship and fails the AppImage on the first library it strips; the same export and reason appear in dist.sh.

dist.sh produces the whole release matrix into dist/: it exports CROSS_CONTAINER_ENGINE=podman, prepends /opt/llvm-mingw/llvm-mingw-ucrt/bin to PATH and sets SKIP_TRUNK=true, then per target cross-builds `oxyromon --features server` plus the eight format-crate CLIs (`cross build -p chd-rs -p cia-rs -p gdi-rs -p nsz-rs -p xdelta-rs -p wux-rs -p xps-rs -p xso-rs`, yielding chdrs, ciars, gdirs, nszrs, wuxrs, xdeltars, xpsrs, xsors) for four Linux targets, x86_64-pc-windows-gnullvm and two apple-darwin targets, packing oxyromon and each CLI as a separate archive — nine per target, .tar.xz for Linux/macOS and .7z for Windows — named with the target triple's vendor field trimmed, and running `cargo clean` between targets.

Cross-compilation keeps the web UI out of the containers: dist.sh exports SKIP_TRUNK=true and Cross.toml passes that variable through to the cross container under [build.env], while `(cd frontend && trunk build --release)` runs on the host at the top of each target iteration because the wasm bundle is target-independent.

The two macOS targets have no upstream cross images: Cross.toml maps aarch64-apple-darwin and x86_64-apple-darwin to ghcr.io/cross-rs/<target>-cross:local, so those images must be built locally before dist.sh can produce Apple artifacts.

Code signing applies only to Apple artifacts: for each darwin target dist.sh runs `rcodesign sign` on oxyromon after the cross build and on each of the eight format CLIs inside the packaging loop, both before tarring, while Linux and Windows artifacts are shipped unsigned.

The Tauri desktop bundle is built for the host only and cannot be cross-compiled, because Tauri links the platform's own webview, which the cross images do not carry and for which no cross toolchain exists; Windows and macOS bundles require running the build on that operating system.

The desktop app ships no separate backend: tauri.conf.json declares externalBin binaries/oxyromon and runs desktop/scripts/stage-sidecar.sh as both beforeDevCommand and beforeBuildCommand; the script resolves the triple from TARGET_TRIPLE or `rustc -vV`, runs `cargo build --release --features server` from the repository root, and copies the binary to desktop/binaries/oxyromon-<triple>[.exe], a generated gitignored directory.

docker.sh tags the container from the package version rather than from git: it reads .package.version out of Cargo.toml with tomlq and builds/pushes alucryd/oxyromon:<version> and :latest from the single Dockerfile using sudo docker.

The automated Docker path is narrower than docker.sh: .github/workflows/docker.yml triggers on push to develop and builds and pushes ./Dockerfile with tags derived by docker/metadata-action from the git ref, so the version-pinned tag exists only after someone runs docker.sh manually.

The single Alpine-based Dockerfile is a self-contained build-and-run image that compiles the web UI inside the image (it does not set SKIP_TRUNK): it installs build-base, curl, musl-dev, rustup and tar, the wasm32-unknown-unknown target and trunk 0.21.14's musl build, runs `cargo install --features server --root /usr --path .`, then removes those packages, the toolchain, caches and source tree. It installs no external format tool, no gcompat and no cmake; GNU tar is for the fetch-webawesome.sh hook.

The image pins runtime paths via environment (OXYROMON_DATA_DIRECTORY=/data, OXYROMON_ROM_DIRECTORY=/roms) with matching VOLUME declarations, but CMD is bare `oxyromon`; since main() only performs work inside `if let Some((subcommand, ...)) = matches.subcommand()`, a container started without an appended subcommand does nothing.

Format crates are published independently of oxyromon — own version, own CHANGELOG.md in oxyromon's format, `<crate>-<version>` git tags — which imposes a hard ordering rule: a crate must be published to crates.io before any oxyromon release that needs its new version, because the root declares each dependency with both `path` and `version` and the root's exclude list keeps `crates/` out of its own tarball.

oxyromon cannot be published while nod points at git, because crates.io rejects git dependencies: it is pinned to tag v2.0.0-alpha.12, with a `ponytail` comment saying to go back to a version requirement before a release, pending a crates.io release past 2.0.0-alpha.9. It is a mandatory dependency (0.25.0 deleted the optional nod feature), so this is the only git-sourced dependency left blocking publication — sevenz-rust2 is back to a plain `version = "0.24.0"` requirement with the zstd feature.

The published crate is deliberately smaller than the checkout: frontend/ and desktop/ are publish = false standalone crates with their own [workspace], and Cargo.toml excludes .github/, crates/, dist/ and tests/, so a crates.io install builds without the nested frontend package — the case build.rs guards by asserting frontend/ exists and by always creating target/assets for rust-embed.

AGENTS.md makes documentation part of every change rather than part of the release: each notable change must update the relevant README.md command section to match real --help output and add a CHANGELOG.md entry under the current version's Features/Changes/Improvements/Fixes section, creating that version's block if absent, where 'current version' is the version field in Cargo.toml.

The release version is duplicated across four manifests that nothing checks against one another — Cargo.toml, frontend/Cargo.toml, desktop/Cargo.toml and desktop/tauri.conf.json (all 0.25.0) — while docker.sh derives its tags from the root value alone, so a bump must update all four by hand.

Because sqlx macros verify queries at compile time, changed queries require `cargo sqlx prepare -- --all-targets --features server` to refresh the committed .sqlx/ offline data; a change left unprepared forces a live DATABASE_URL, which the cross containers and the Docker build do not provide, so it breaks the release matrix rather than only a developer's machine.

No workflow builds or publishes release artifacts: continuous_integration.yml (push/PR to master and develop) sets SKIP_TRUNK=true with TRUNK_VERSION pinned to 0.21.14, builds the web UI once, runs clippy twice — workspace with oxyromon/server, and --no-default-features --features use-rustls,mcp so mcp-only builds cannot rot — then `cargo build --release --features server` and workspace coverage uploaded to Codecov, installing mame-tools, xdelta3 and ffmpeg so the crates' reference-tool interop tests run instead of skipping.

Release archives need no external tool installed beside them: `oxyromon info` lists chd-rs, cia-rs, xso-rs, xps-rs, xdelta-rs, nsz-rs, wux-rs, sevenz-rust2 and nod, every one returning "built-in" from get_version() (nsz-rs and wux-rs adding a note when their keys are missing), and the README states that every format is handled in-process.

Shipping binaries are shaped by three divergent profiles: the root [profile.release] uses lto = "thin", codegen-units = 1, strip = true and panic = "abort" for oxyromon and the format CLIs, while frontend and desktop each declare their own size-oriented opt-level = "z" profiles because they are standalone crates outside the workspace.

test.sh is now a single coverage pass — `cargo llvm-cov --workspace --features oxyromon/server --lcov --output-path lcov.info` — identical to the command CI runs, and it covers the format crates because --workspace includes crates/*. The former second pass with oxyromon/nod and oxyromon/sevenz is gone; those features were deleted in 0.25.0 when RVZ/WBFS and 7z/ZIP support became unconditional, so those feature names would fail to resolve.

Each format crate ships its CLI behind a default `cli` feature (`[[bin]] required-features = ["cli"]` in all six manifests), and oxyromon depends on them with `default-features = false`, so the six binaries exist only when the crates are built directly — which is exactly what dist.sh's `cross build -p chd-rs -p gdi-rs …` step does, and why the root build never pulls clap/indicatif into the CLI.

0.25.0 replaced the external chdman tool with the in-repo chd-rs crate (CHD for CDs, DVDs, hard disks and LaserDiscs, output interchangeable with chdman 0.289) and added its CLI chdrs to the release archives — the same pattern the changelog records for xpsrs/xdeltars in 0.25.0 and gdirs/nszrs/xsors in 0.24.0 — so each port simultaneously removes an external tool and adds one shipped binary to the matrix. Root publishes are tagged 0.x while crate publishes get their own <crate>-<version> tags (for example nsz-rs-0.3.0).
A .dockerignore keeps .git, .github, graft/, openwiki/, plans/, port/, tests/, desktop/, target/ and the frontend build outputs out of the Docker build context, keeping only the build inputs.
